transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Yeah… um, I guess the main reason is work. I’m a cashier, and lately at the register I keep getting caught doing these things that don’t really fit what’s happening. Like a customer will be standing there waiting to pay, and instead of just scanning or opening the drawer like I’m supposed to, I’ll start tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or I’ll just sort of freeze with my hand over the cash drawer. I know it sounds strange when I say it out loud, but in the moment I get stuck.

It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult. I can see the customer waiting, I can see the line, and part of me knows, “Okay, move, finish the transaction,” but then I’m just… doing this other thing, or not moving at all. Last week it happened enough that my supervisor wrote me up, and that’s what really pushed me to come in. I’ve worked as a cashier a long time, and getting written up for something like that was embarrassing. I don’t want to lose my job over it.
Do you feel anxious or distressed when these behaviors happen, or do they feel like something you need to do in order to prevent something bad from happening?

It’s not exactly like I’m thinking, “If I don’t tap the scanner, something terrible will happen.” It doesn’t feel that clear or, I don’t know, organized like that. It’s more that I’m standing there at the register and I get caught in it — like the customer is right there, the total is on the screen, I know I’m supposed to take the money or open the drawer, and then my hand just sort of stays there, or I start tapping the scanner in this little pattern.

I do get distressed, but usually because I can see it’s not matching the moment. Like I know the person is waiting, and I can feel the line building up, and then I’m thinking, “Why am I doing this? Just move.” But it’s like I’m stuck for a bit. Last week it happened enough that my supervisor wrote me up, and that really bothered me. It’s embarrassing, because I’ve done cashier work a long time, and now I’m getting in trouble for freezing or doing these odd little things when I should just be finishing the transaction.
When these episodes happen at work, do you have any particular thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that feel intrusive or unwanted?

I don’t know if I’d call them thoughts or images, exactly. That’s the part I have trouble explaining. It’s not like some picture pops into my head, or a sentence like, “Do this now,” or anything that clear. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way.

It’s more like… I’m in the middle of the transaction, and everything should be automatic because I’ve done this for years — scan, total, take the money, give change — and then suddenly that normal flow gets interrupted. I’ll get this pull toward the tapping, or I’ll just sort of hang there with my hand not doing what it’s supposed to do. But if you asked me what I was thinking right then, a lot of times I’d say I’m mostly thinking, “Why am I stuck?” or “The customer is waiting,” after it’s already happening.

So, intrusive in the sense that I don’t want it and it gets in the way, yes. But not intrusive like a specific unwanted thought or mental picture that I can point to. It’s more blank or jammed up, if that makes sense.
When you find yourself tapping the scanner or freezing at the register, do you feel like you have to do it a certain way or for a certain number of times, even if you can’t explain why?

Yeah… sort of, but not in a neat way like counting to five or ten. It’s not like I’ve got a rule in my head that says, “Tap it exactly three times or else.” It’s more that I’ll start tapping the scanner in a pattern, and while I’m doing it, it feels like I’m caught in that pattern for a moment. Like my hand is doing that instead of doing the normal cashier thing, which would be scanning the item or opening the drawer or handing back change.

And sometimes it’s not tapping, it’s the freezing part that’s worse. I’ll have my hand over the cash drawer, and the customer is right there, waiting, and I know the transaction needs to keep moving, but I just stop. I can see the whole thing happening, which makes it embarrassing, because it doesn’t fit what’s going on. It’s like the moment calls for one action, and I’m doing something else, or nothing at all.

That’s basically why I came in. It’s been happening at the register enough that last week my supervisor wrote me up for it. I’ve been a cashier a long time, so being written up because I’m tapping the scanner or freezing while someone is waiting… it really shook me.
Do you ever feel a strong internal pressure or need to perform the tapping or freezing behavior in a specific way, even if you can’t explain why?

Yeah, I mean… there is a pressure, but I don’t know if I’d call it a “need” exactly, like a planned thing. It’s more like I get stuck in it. At the register, the moment is very obvious — the customer is standing there, the total is up, I should be taking the money or opening the drawer or handing back change — and instead I’ll be tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand will just freeze over the cash drawer.

And while it’s happening, it feels like I can’t just smoothly switch back to what I’m supposed to be doing. It doesn’t feel like I chose it, but it also doesn’t feel like I can explain why it has to happen that way. It’s just… my body is doing something that doesn’t fit the moment, and I’m aware of it, which makes it worse because the person is waiting.

That’s really why I came in. It’s been happening enough at work that last week my supervisor wrote me up for it. I’ve been doing cashier work a long time, so being written up because I’m tapping the scanner or freezing there while someone is waiting was really upsetting.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself doing repetitive behaviors or feeling the need to do things a certain way, even if you can’t explain why?

Outside of work… I mean, not in the same way that it’s been showing up at the register. That’s where it really stands out, because there’s a job I’m supposed to be doing right then, and the customer is right there watching, so when I get stuck it’s obvious.

At home, I might repeat something here or there, but I don’t know if I’d call it the same problem. The reason I came in is more because at work I keep getting caught doing things that just don’t fit the moment — like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or freezing with my hand over the cash drawer when I’m supposed to be giving change or finishing the sale. And it’s not private there. The customer is waiting, the line can back up, and then I’m aware that I’m just… stuck.

Last week my supervisor wrote me up for it, and that really bothered me, because I’ve been a cashier a long time. I’m not new at it. So outside of work, I’m not sure I’ve noticed it as much, but at the register it’s become enough of a problem that I couldn’t just ignore it anymore.
After you tap the scanner or freeze at the register, do you feel any relief from the discomfort you felt before doing it, or does the distress usually keep going or even get worse?

I don’t really get relief from it, no. That’s kind of the thing — it’s not like I tap the scanner and then suddenly I feel better, or like some tension goes away and I can move on cleanly. If anything, once I realize I’ve done it, or I realize I’ve frozen there with my hand over the drawer while the customer is waiting, I feel more upset, because now I’m aware that I’m doing something that doesn’t fit the moment.

Like, the register has a rhythm to it. Scan the item, tell them the total, take the money, open the drawer, give change, hand them the receipt. I know all that. I’ve done it for years. But then I get stuck in this little tapping pattern on the scanner, or I just stop with my hand hovering there, and the whole normal sequence gets interrupted. And the customer is looking at me, and sometimes I can feel the line behind them, and it’s like the distress doesn’t go away — it kind of builds because I know I’m holding things up.

That’s why I came in, really. It’s been happening enough at the register that last week my supervisor wrote me up for it. I’ve been a cashier a long time, so getting written up because I’m tapping or freezing instead of just finishing the sale… that really bothered me. So no, I wouldn’t say there’s relief. It mostly just makes me feel stuck and embarrassed, and then I have to try to pull myself back into what I was supposed to be doing.
Before you start tapping the scanner or freezing at the register, do you ever feel an uncomfortable sensation, urge, or need that seems to lead into the behavior?

Before it happens… I’m not sure I’d call it an urge exactly. That’s what makes it hard to explain. It’s not like I’m standing there thinking, “I have to tap the scanner now,” or “I need to freeze my hand over the drawer.” It doesn’t feel that organized.

It’s more like I’m in the middle of the normal cashier routine — scan, total, take the money, open the drawer — and then I just get caught. I’ll start tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand will stop over the cash drawer, and it doesn’t fit what’s supposed to be happening. The customer is right there waiting, so I know I should be moving on, but for a moment I’m just stuck in that behavior.

I guess there might be some kind of tension right before it, but I don’t know how to describe it as a sensation or a need. The main thing is that at the register I keep doing these things that interrupt the sale, and it’s become noticeable enough that last week my supervisor wrote me up for it. That’s really what scared me into coming in, because I’ve done this job for years and I shouldn’t be freezing there or tapping the scanner while someone is waiting.

Before your hand starts tapping the scanner or freezing at the register, do you ever notice a strange or uncomfortable feeling in your body that seems to lead into the behavior, like a tingling, pressure, or need for something to feel 'just right'?

I don’t know that I notice a body feeling like that, like tingling or pressure, exactly. I’ve been trying to think about it because you’ve asked it a couple different ways, and I get why you’re asking, but it doesn’t feel like there’s this clear sensation beforehand where I can say, “Oh, here it comes.”

What I notice more is what happens at the register. I’ll be in the middle of the sale, doing the normal steps I’ve done for years, and then suddenly I’m not doing the next step. I’m tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or my hand is just sort of frozen over the cash drawer, and the customer is standing there waiting for me to finish. It doesn’t match the moment. That’s the part that bothers me.

And it’s not like I’m waiting for something to feel “just right,” at least not in a way I can explain. It’s more like I get stuck doing something that doesn’t belong there, and then I realize the line is held up or the person is looking at me. Last week it got bad enough that my supervisor wrote me up, and that’s really what made me come in, because I’ve been doing this job a long time and I shouldn’t be getting stuck tapping the scanner or hovering over the drawer instead of just finishing the transaction.
